items.title: Phil Schaap interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: my illustrious cousin, you know, hit big time sports right then and started like free ticket city. That would be Dick Schaap.

ctx.x: Yeah. She may not — I may be making her out to be more shrewish, she was a zany Bohemian jazz lover. But she didn’t want — I guess she wanted the best for me and she had to figure out what the best was at the time. So I got involved in singing with my boy soprano in the major music program of the New York City public school system which was an excellent program in those days. Always yearning to be in the instrumental

program and the enriched program — they call it SPE — or they called it I gather, I have no idea whether it still exists in the New York City public school system. But SPE is a special program for good, gifted students. But the E meant there’d be some music component. Enriched is what it stood for. And you either went into the band or you went into the chorus. And I wanted that band bad. But I’d been singing on an enriched music program with this boy soprano fourth, fifth and sixth grade because I had done okay…

And Billy Crystal liked that, and Dick Schaap liked that because it was so odd, and Bernhardt, he can’t believe, I’m the only guy he meets who doesn’t know his famous nephew and does know his late brother.
